titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 125 — entering the Hall of the Two Truths
part: Spell 125 — entering the Hall of the Two Truths (Plates 30 and 29)
about: The introduction to Spell 125: Ani arrives at the Hall of the Two Truths, where the dead are judged, greets Osiris, and claims his purity by listing the holy places he has been to and the secret things he has seen; then Anubis, keeper of the door, questions him, and he must name the door and its two leaves before he may pass. Budge prints lines 1–18 under Plate 30 and then goes back to Plate 29 for lines 19–28; on the papyrus the spell goes on to the 42 declarations (Plates 31–32). Several passages are obscure or garbled in Ani's copy, and the notes say where.

sentences.l: spell · of · entering · into · the-hall · of-the-Two-Truths · adoring · Osiris · foremost · of-the-West
sentences.i: Spell for entering the Hall of the Two Truths. Adoring Osiris, Foremost of the West.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes the title in red — rꜣ n ꜥq r, and dwꜣ — while the names of the hall and of the god stand in black. rꜣ is the mouth (r) with its stroke, 'utterance, spell'; n is the genitive 'of'. ꜥq 'enter' is the cormorant (ꜥq) with q as complement and the walking legs as classifier of motion; r 'into'. wsḫt 'broad hall' is spelled w-s-ḫ-t, with the hall sign as classifier and its t written again after it. mꜣꜥti 'the Two Truths' is the sickle (mꜣ) before the plinth (mꜣꜥ), t and the two strokes (-ti, the dual), and its classifiers double everything: two feathers of Maat, two cobra-goddesses, two town signs — Truth as a pair of goddesses and as a place. dwꜣ 'adore' is hand d and lasso wꜣ with a man raising his arms. wsir 'Osiris' is the seat (ws) and the eye (ir); ḫnty 'foremost' the three jars ḫnt with n, t and the y-strokes; imntt 'the West' the emblem of the West with t, t and the hill-country sign. This heading covers all of Spell 125: in this hall the heart is weighed, and the first thing the dead man does there is praise Osiris, king of the dead.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · scribe · Ani · true-of-voice
sentences.i: Words spoken by the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice:
sentences.n: ḏd in, in red, is the standing formula that brings in a speech: ḏd 'say' (cobra ḏ + hand d; the print sets the hand under the curve of the cobra) and in 'by', the particle that names the speaker (reed i + water n). Wsir Ani, 'the Osiris Ani': the dead man carries the god's name, as one who will rise from death as Osiris did. sš 'scribe' is the scribe's palette, water-pot and pen alone. ꜣny 'Ani' is vulture ꜣ, water n and two reeds (y), with the seated man as classifier; the three small strokes under ꜣ-n belong to the usual writing of his name and are not read. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw (plinth mꜣꜥ + oar ḫrw) is 'true of voice': one whose words have been found true at the judgement, that is, vindicated. It follows Ani's name nearly every time.

sentences.l: have-come · I · here · to · see · beauty · your
sentences.i: I have come here to see your beauty.
sentences.n: ii·n·i 'I have come' is the sḏm·n·f, the past/perfect form: the verb ii 'come' (the reed-leaf ii with a reed i as complement and the walking legs), then the n that marks the form, then the seated man ·i 'I'. The next group is doubtful in the print: a long column-shaped sign over the road sign. It is read here as ꜥꜣ 'here, hither' (the column ꜥꜣ) with the road as classifier of direction; Budge takes it as a verb of motion. r + infinitive gives purpose: r mꜣꜣ 'to see' (sickle mꜣ, the eye as classifier, and vultures for ꜣ). nfrw 'beauty' is the heart-and-windpipe sign nfr written three times — the plural, used for an abstract — and ·k (the basket) is 'your': Ani speaks to Osiris.

sentences.l: two-arms · my · in · praise · of · name · your · true
sentences.i: My arms are (raised) in praise of your true name.
sentences.n: A sentence with no verb: the subject ꜥwy·i 'my two arms' and the adverbial phrase m iꜣw 'in praise' as its predicate. ꜥwy is the arm (ꜥ) written twice for the dual, with the dual strokes (y) and w; ·i 'my'. iꜣw 'praise, adoration' is reed i, vulture ꜣ, quail chick w, with the man raising his arms in worship as classifier. rn·k 'your name' (mouth r, water n, basket ·k). mꜣꜥ 'true' (sickle and plinth again) comes after the noun and its suffix, as Egyptian adjectives do. 'Raised' is not written: raised arms were simply the posture of praise. To know and praise a god's true name gave a claim on him.

sentences.l: have-come · I · here · not · came-into-being · cedar · not · (yet)-born · acacia · not · created · ground · tamarisk
sentences.i: I have come here, (where) the cedar has not come into being, the acacia has not (yet) been born, and the ground has not brought forth the tamarisk.
sentences.n: Three negative clauses follow ii·n·i ꜥꜣ. n ḫpr ꜥš: the negative n (two arms spread, D35), ḫpr 'come into being' (the scarab ḫpr, with r as complement), and ꜥš 'cedar' (arm ꜥ, pool š and a wood classifier whose printed form is uncertain; Budge adds a query). n ms·t šndt: msi 'give birth, be born' (the three fox-skins ms, s as complement, a woman giving birth as classifier) carries a t: this is the n sḏmt·f form, 'has not yet …'. šndt 'acacia' is the looped cord šn, d, t and a tree. The third n is Budge's restoration of damage. qmꜣw 'create, produce' (q, sickle mꜣ, vulture ꜣ, then a w the grammar does not need, and a bird on a perch that the print does not render cleanly), sꜣtw 'ground, soil' (pintail duck sꜣ, t, land sign, w), isr 'tamarisk' (i, s, r, tree, plural). What the clauses describe is uncertain: a place where no tree grows, or, with 'not yet', a time before the first trees. Ani's copy is obscure here.

sentences.l: when · entered · I · into · the-place · of-secret-things · … · spoke · I · with · Seth
sentences.i: When I entered the place of secret things, I spoke with Seth.
sentences.n: ir + sḏm·f at the head of a sentence is 'when, if': ir ꜥq·i 'when I entered'. st 'place, seat' is the seat sign (st) with t and the house as classifier. štꜣw 'secret things' is pool š, loaf t, and for ꜣ a small pot that Budge's type gives the shape of the nw-pot (W24) — it stands for ꜣ in this word every time in the spell — then the crossed sticks and the papyrus roll as classifiers of the abstract, and the plural strokes. In ḏd·t·i the first sign is printed as a plain rod (coded U28, an approximation) where the cobra ḏ is expected; then d, a t, the man with his hand to his mouth (speech), plural strokes and ·i. iw followed by ḏd·t·i is not a regular construction (the t looks like that of the sḏmt·f form); Budge takes the whole as 'I have spoken', and that is followed here. ḥnꜥ 'with' (wick ḥ, water n, arm ꜥ). Seth's name is written s-t with a small rectangle, a staff and the seated god: only s and t are read, and the name is taken as stẖ, Seth (Budge: Sut), the god who killed Osiris.

morph.gloss: when, if (particle at the head of a clause)

sentences.l: companion(?) · my · drew-near · to-me · covered · face · his · fallen · upon · things · secret
sentences.i: My companion(?) drew near to me, his face covered, fallen upon the secret things.
sentences.n: ḫnm is the jug ḫnm with ḫ, n and m as complements and the nose as classifier — the verb 'smell, be joined with'. With ·i it is taken here as a noun, 'my companion', which is doubtful (Budge queries it too). tkn 'come near' (t, k, n, walking legs) comes after its subject, and tkn m is 'come near to': im·i is m 'in, at' with ·i, for m becomes im before a suffix. ḥbs 'clothe, cover' (ḥ, b, s and a fringed cloth) stands before ḥr·f 'his face' (the face with its stroke and ·f): 'covered (was) his face'. ḫrw 'fallen' is ḫr 'fall' (ḫ, r) with the w of the stative and a falling man as classifier. ḫt štꜣw 'secret things': ḫt 'thing' is placenta ḫ, t and the papyrus roll. Whose face is covered — Seth's or the companion's — the text does not say; the whole passage is obscure.

morph.gloss: in, at, near — m takes the form im before a suffix

sentences.l: and · entered · he · into · the-house · of-Osiris
sentences.i: He entered the house of Osiris
sentences.n: iw·f ꜥq·f: the particle iw (reed i, quail chick w) with its subject ·f (the horned viper), then the sḏm·f ꜥq·f 'he entered'. The account has moved into the third person. pr 'house' is the plan of a house with its stroke, the word written as a picture; pr wsir, 'the house of Osiris', is his temple or domain below.

sentences.l: and · saw · he · secret-things · which · in · it
sentences.i: and he saw the secret things that are in it.
sentences.n: mꜣꜣ·f 'he saw' puts the eye first, then the sickle mꜣ and a vulture ꜣ (the print sets eye and sickle as a ligature). nty 'which, that' is the relative adjective (water n, loaf t, two strokes y), and im·f 'in it' is m with ·f, which here refers to the house.

morph.gloss: in — m takes the form im before a suffix

sentences.l: the-council · of · the-gateways · (is) · as · spirits
sentences.i: The council of the gateways are spirits.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏꜣ-ꜣ-t-ḏꜣ-s; read ḏꜣḏꜣt. ḏꜣḏꜣt 'council, tribunal' is the fire-drill ḏꜣ twice, with ꜣ (again the small pot) and t, the plural strokes and the seated god as classifiers; the bolt s after the second ḏꜣ has no place in the word. nt is the feminine form of the genitive 'of' (n + t), agreeing with ḏꜣḏꜣt. sbḫyt 'gateways' (s, b, ḫ, two reeds, t, plural strokes) are the portals of the world below. iw + noun + m-phrase says what the subject is: m ꜣḫw 'as spirits' — the ꜣḫ, written with the crested ibis, is the glorified, effective dead. Spirits keep the gates.

sentences.l: said · by · Anubis · to · sides · his-two · voice · of-a-man · coming · from · Egypt
sentences.i: Anubis said to those on either side of him: 'The voice of a man who comes from Egypt!'
sentences.n: ḏd in brings in a new speaker (not in red this time). inpw 'Anubis' is reed i, water n, stool p, quail chick w and the seated god. gs 'side' (the half-loaf sign) with its stroke, then ·f, then the two strokes y: the dual ending is written after the suffix, gs·fy 'his two sides', and n gs·fy is 'to (those at) his two sides'. ḫrw 'voice' is the oar with w and the man with hand to mouth; s 'man' is the bolt with stroke and seated man (the genitive is direct: 'voice of a man'). iw 'coming' is a participle written with the walking legs, w, and the legs again. tꜣ-mri 'Egypt' is the land sign tꜣ, the hoe mr with r and i, a staff that the print does not render cleanly, and two town signs. Anubis, guardian of the cemetery, is the doorkeeper here, and he speaks about the newcomer to the gods beside him.

sentences.l: he · knows · roads · our · towns · our
sentences.i: He knows our roads and our towns.
sentences.n: iw·f with the stative: rḫw 'he knows' (mouth r, placenta ḫ, the w of the stative, and the papyrus roll for something abstract). wꜣwt 'roads' is the road sign with t; ·n 'our', the 1st person plural suffix, is water n with the plural strokes (and a further stroke). dmiw 'towns' is d with the threshing-floor sign mi, reed i, the land sign and stroke; again ·n 'our'. The two nouns stand side by side without 'and'.

sentences.l: content · I · smell · I · scent · his · as · one · of · you
sentences.i: I am content: I smell his scent as (that of) one of you.
sentences.n: ḥtp·kwi is the stative of ḥtp 'be content, at peace': the offering table ḥtp with t and p, an extra t, and the 1st singular ending ·kwi written k, a coiled w and a stroke for i. snsn 'smell, breathe' is two arrowheads sn (the print is not clear); the small horned head after them is uncertain and taken as classifier. sty 'scent' (s, t, y, with a round classifier) + ·f 'his'. wꜥ 'one' is the harpoon wꜥ with ꜥ; im·tn 'of you' is m before the 2nd plural suffix ·tn (t, n, plural strokes). Anubis is still speaking: the newcomer smells like one of the gods.

morph.gloss: of, among — m takes the form im before a suffix

sentences.l: says · he · to-me · I · the-Osiris · scribe · Ani · true-of-voice · in · peace · true-of-voice
sentences.i: He says to me — I am the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice in peace, true of voice.
sentences.n: ḏd·f n·i 'he says to me': ḏd with ·f, and the preposition n 'to' with ·i. What follows is not Anubis's speech but Ani's reply; no question is written, and the scribe may have left one out. ink 'I' is the independent pronoun, here spelled with the nw-pot, k and the seated man, a spelling common in these papyri; ink + noun is the sentence 'I am …'. m ḥtp 'in peace' uses another sign for m (the rib-like Aa15) and the offering table alone for ḥtp. Wsir Ani and mꜣꜥ-ḫrw as at the start; the doubled 'true of voice' is a flourish of the scribe.

sentences.l: have-come · I · here · to · see · gods · great · live · I · on · offerings · which-are-in · kas · their
sentences.i: I have come here to see the great gods, and I live on the offerings that are among their kas.
sentences.n: The first clause repeats line 2. nṯrw 'gods' is the god's flag nṯr written three times for the plural; ꜥꜣw 'great' follows it (column ꜥꜣ with ꜥ and ꜣ as complements, plural). ꜥnḫ·i 'I live' is the ankh (ꜥnḫ) with n and ḫ as complements; ꜥnḫ m is 'live on (food)'. ḥtpwt 'offerings' is ḥtp with t and p, the feminine plural t, a loaf and plural strokes. imyw (the crossed planks im, w, plural) is the nisba 'who/which are in'. kꜣw·sn 'their kas' is the raised arms kꜣ with the 3rd plural ·sn (s, n, plural strokes). The link between the offerings and the kas is loose (imyw is masculine, ḥtpwt feminine), and kꜣw can also mean 'food', so the sense is not sure. The ka, the life-force, was what received the offerings.

sentences.l: have-been · I · at · the-borders · of-the-Ram · lord · of-Mendes
sentences.i: I have been at the borders of the Ram, lord of Mendes.
sentences.n: wn·n·i is the sḏm·n·f of wnn 'be' (the hare wn with n as complement, then the n of the form and ·i): 'I have been'. From here Ani lists the holy places he has visited, most of them with wn·n·i. ḏrw 'limits, borders' (the plant ḏr with r, the road sign and plural). bꜣ, the Ram (the word is 'soul'), has a small first sign that the print gives like a fire-altar — doubtful — and the ram as classifier. nb 'lord' is the basket. ḏdt is the djed-pillar twice with d, t and the town sign: with its t it is Djedet, Mendes in the Delta, city of the Ram, not Djedu (Busiris), although Budge renders both as Tattu.

sentences.l: let · he · come-forth · I · as · the-Bennu · so-that · speak · I
sentences.i: He let me come forth as the Bennu-bird, so that I might speak.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes b-n-t-w; read bnw, the Bennu, with the heron as classifier. di·f (the giving arm di, + ·f) followed by a second sḏm·f, pr·i 'that I go out', is the causative 'he caused me to come forth, he let me come forth'; pri 'go out' is the house sign pr with r and the walking legs. r ḏd·t·i: r with the sḏmt·f form strictly means 'until I speak'; here it reads more easily as purpose. The first sign of ḏd·t·i is again the plain rod printed for the cobra ḏ (U28, an approximation). The Bennu, the sun's heron of Heliopolis, is the very image of coming forth into the day.

morph.gloss: until, so that (with the sḏmt·f form)

sentences.l: have-been · I · in · the-river
sentences.i: I have been in the river.
sentences.n: itrw 'river' (reed i, t, r, w) has two water classifiers, the three ripples and the canal. Budge's 'water of the river' is one word.

sentences.l: offered · I · with · incense
sentences.i: I have made offering with incense.
sentences.n: wdn 'offer, make offering' is spelled w-d-n with a classifier the print leaves uncertain and the papyrus roll; without the n of the past it is the sḏm·f, here telling of the past. m 'with'. snṯr 'incense' (literally 'what makes divine') is written with the god's flag first, in honour, then sn (the arrowhead), t, r and plural strokes; Budge prints the flag as a group of its own, and it is joined here into the one word.

sentences.l: went(?) · I · by · the-acacia · of · the-children
sentences.i: I made my way(?) by the acacia of the children.
sentences.n: sm (bolt s, the plant sm, m, walking legs) has a classifier of motion and is taken as 'go, make one's way'; the verb is not well known and the reading of its main sign is uncertain in the print. šndt 'acacia', as on line 3, here with n as complement. ẖrdw 'children' is the seated child with his hand to his mouth, with a seated man and woman and plural strokes. What 'the acacia of the children' was is not known; Budge queries it too.

sentences.l: have-been · I · in · Abydos · in · the-House-of-Satet
sentences.i: I have been in Abydos, in the House of Satet.
sentences.n: ꜣbḏw 'Abydos' is the emblem of the East (ꜣb) with b as complement, a round sign where the hill sign ḏw is expected (coded Aa2 from the print; read ḏw), and the desert-town sign. pr-sṯt is 'the House of Satet': the house with its stroke, the pierced hide sṯ (Budge prints a query beside it), t, t, and a cobra-goddess as classifier. Abydos was Osiris's own city; a shrine of Satet, goddess of the First Cataract, is unexpected there, and the name is uncertain.

sentences.l: sank · I · the-boat · of · the-enemies
sentences.i: I sank the boat of the enemies.
sentences.n: iw + sḏm·n·f. smḥ 'cause to sink' is the causative s + mḥ 'be drowned': bolt s, then a looped sign (coded V6 from the print) that stands where the whip mḥ is needed, ḥ as complement, two small strokes and the boat as classifier; then the n of the past and ·i. wiꜣ 'boat, bark' (w, i, boat; ꜣ not written). ḫftyw 'enemies' is ḫ, f, t and the vulture ꜣ standing for the ending -y, with a kneeling man as classifier. The enemies are those of Osiris and of the sun.

sentences.l: I · crossed · over · the-lake · in · the-Neshmet-bark
sentences.i: I crossed the lake in the Neshmet-bark.
sentences.n: iw·i (here the stroke stands for ·i) + the stative ḏꜣ·kwi 'I crossed (by water)': the fire-drill ḏꜣ with ꜣ, the boat and a stroke; of the ending ·kwi only k is written. š 'lake' is the pool with a stroke and a land sign. nšmt (n, š, m, t, boat) is the Neshmet, the bark of Osiris at Abydos in which his image sailed at his festival.

sentences.l: have-seen · I · the-nobles · of-Kem-wer
sentences.i: I have seen the nobles of Kem-wer.
sentences.n: mꜣꜣ·n·i 'I have seen', the sḏm·n·f. sꜥḥw 'nobles, dignitaries' (s, ꜥ, ḥ, then an ankh-like sign that is not read, a man of rank, plural). The genitive is direct, noun + noun. km-wr 'the Great Black' is the crocodile-skin km with m, the swallow wr with r, a bull and the town sign — a sacred place with a bull-cult (Budge: Qem-ur).

sentences.l: have-been · I · in · Busiris · silenced · I
sentences.i: I have been in Busiris, and I have made silence.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes sgrw·n·i, with a w that has no place in the form; read sgr·n·i. ḏdw 'Busiris' (the djed-pillar ḏd, d, w, town) is Osiris's city in the Delta, met already in the Confession. sgr 'make silent' is the causative of gr 'be silent': bolt s, jar-stand g, r, the stray w, and the man with hand to mouth. No object is written: 'I have made (all) silent'; Budge takes it as falling silent oneself.

sentences.l: placed · I · the-image(?) · of-the-god · on · feet · his-two
sentences.i: I have set the image of the god upon his feet.
sentences.n: di·n·i 'I have placed' (giving arm di, n, ·i). sḫm 'power; sacred image' is the sceptre sḫm with m and a low flat sign printed as U15 (the sledge) where the sense expects the forearm with stick (D40), the classifier of force and effort; the same printed sign comes again in ḥbs, ḥꜣw, ḫr-sk and ṯsw below. nṯr 'god' is the flag with the seated god. rd·fy: mouth r, d, the two legs, ·f, and the dual strokes y written after the suffix — 'his two feet'. Whether sḫm here is the god's image or his power is not sure; 'image' suits 'set upon his feet'. The numeral of line 13 stands inside this word in Budge's print.

sentences.l: have-been · I · in · the-House-of-Him-upon-his-Mountain · have-seen · I · the-foremost · of-the-temple
sentences.i: I have been in the House of Him-who-is-upon-his-Mountain; I have seen the Foremost of the Temple.
sentences.n: pr-tp-ḏw-f: pr 'house', tp 'head, top' (the head), ḏw 'mountain', then a shrine façade, f and the seated god — 'the House of Him upon his Mountain', that is of Anubis, whose title this is (Budge: Per-tep-tu-f). ḫnty 'foremost', as in the title. ḥwt-nṯr 'temple' (lit. 'mansion of the god') is written with the god's flag first, in honour, then the enclosure ḥwt, which is read with doubt (Budge queries it); Budge prints two groups, joined here as one word.

sentences.l: I · entered · into · the-House-of-Osiris · uncovered(?) · I · the-head-cloths · of · him-who · (is) · there
sentences.i: I entered the House of Osiris, and I took off(?) the head-cloths of him who is there.
sentences.n: iw·i ꜥq·kwi: iw with ·i and the stative ꜥq·kwi 'I (have) entered', the ending written k, w and the seated man. pr-wsir 'the House of Osiris' writes the eye before the seat (the two signs of wsir change places) with the god as classifier; it is also the Egyptian name of Busiris. kfꜣ (k, f, ꜣ, the hind-quarters sign and a cloth) belongs with kf 'uncover, strip'; the cloth shows it concerns garments, but whether Ani takes the head-cloths off or wraps himself in them is not clear — Budge takes it as draping himself. ꜥfnwt 'head-cloths' (ꜥ, f, n, t, w, cloth, plural). n nty im 'of him who is there': the genitive n, nty used as a noun, and the adverb im 'there'. The numeral of line 14 stands inside pr-wsir in Budge's print.

sentences.l: I · entered · into · Rosetau · have-seen · I · secret-things · which · (are) · there
sentences.i: I entered Rosetau, and I have seen the secret things that are there.
sentences.n: Of the stative ending only k is written (Budge brackets the rest in his transliteration). rꜣ-sṯꜣw, Rosetau, is the mouth rꜣ with its stroke, the coil sṯꜣ, plural strokes and the desert sign: the realm of Sokar in the cemetery near Giza, met already in the Confession. štꜣw nty im 'the secret things that are there', as before.

sentences.l: hid · I · found · I · a-way-through(?)
sentences.i: I hid myself, and I found a way through(?).
sentences.n: imn 'hide' (reed i, the gaming-board mn with n, a man and the papyrus roll as classifiers) + n + ·i: 'I hid'; no object is written, so 'I hid (myself)'. gm 'find' is the ibis gm with m; gm·n·i 'I found'. tš (t, š, crossed sticks, walking legs) is uncertain: the known word tš 'boundary, district' fits ill with the walking legs, which point to something walked through, a way or passage.

sentences.l: I · went-down · to · An-arutef · clothed · I · (with) · what · (is) · there · over · nakedness
sentences.i: I went down to An-arutef, and I covered (my) nakedness with what is there.
sentences.n: hꜣ·kwi 'I went down', the stative of hꜣi 'descend' (courtyard h, vulture ꜣ, walking legs; of the ending only k is written). n-iꜣrrd-f is a holy place of Osiris: the negative n, reed i, vulture ꜣ, r, r, the bowstring rd, a house, f and the town sign. The name looks like n rd·f 'it does not grow', but its exact reading is uncertain (Budge: An-aarut-f). ḥbs·n·i 'I clothed' (ḥ, b, s, cloth, and the low sign printed U15 for the forearm with stick); nty im 'what is there' is its object; ḥr ḥꜣw 'over nakedness': the papyrus clump ḥꜣ with ꜣ, w, cloth and again the U15 sign. No 'my' is written.

sentences.l: put · I · myrrh · of · women · in · the-circuit(?) · of · the-common-folk
sentences.i: I have put the myrrh of women in the circuit(?) of the common folk.
sentences.n: rdi·n·i: rdi 'give, put' in its full writing (mouth r + giving arm), the n of the past, ·i — 'I have given, put'. Budge reads a passive, 'was given to me', which the signs do not show. ꜥntyw 'myrrh' (ꜥ, n, t, the vulture ꜣ for the ending -yw as in ḫftyw, a jar, plural). ḥmwt 'women' (the ḥm sign, t, seated woman, plural). šnw (looped cord šn, n, the pot nw, w, land sign) is 'circuit, surrounding region'; rḫyt 'common folk' is the lapwing with t and plural. The sentence is one of the least clear in Ani's copy, and the rendering is a bare guess.

sentences.l: behold · Seth · told(?) · me · these-things · concerning · him
sentences.i: See, Seth has told me(?) the things concerning himself.
sentences.n: mk 'behold' is written with the owl and the arm joined in a ligature (m with ꜥ, a later spelling, which gives Budge's māk) and the basket k. Seth's name is now the staff-sign with w and t (swt, Budge's Sut). ḏdw·i (cobra ḏ, hand d, w, ·i) is not clear: Budge takes it as 'spoke to me'; with the w it could be the passive 'I was told'. nꜣ (water n, vulture ꜣ) is the demonstrative 'these (things)'; ḥr·f 'concerning him'.

sentences.l: said · I · not · exists · balance · your · in · midst · our
sentences.i: I said: 'There is no balance for you (?) in our midst.'
sentences.n: ḏd·i 'I said' (sḏm·f). The n after it is taken as the negative, and n wn as 'there is not': wn (the hare with n) is the verb 'be, exist'. Budge leaves the n untranslated and reads a wish ('let your weighing be …'); both readings are possible and the passage is obscure. mḫꜣt 'balance, scales' is again written with the owl-and-arm ligature (a later spelling with ꜥ), the balance itself, ꜣ, two strokes and the papyrus roll; ·k 'your'. m ḥry-ib·n 'in our midst': ḥry-ib, literally 'what is upon the heart', is 'middle' — the face ḥr with r and the y-strokes, then the heart ib, and ·n 'our'. Budge prints the y-strokes in the group with ib; the two groups are joined here as one word.

sentences.l: said · by · the-majesty · of · Anubis
sentences.i: Words spoken by the Majesty of Anubis:
sentences.n: ḏd in is written in red. ḥm 'majesty' is the club-shaped sign ḥm with its stroke; 'the Majesty of X' is the court style used of gods as of kings. Anubis now has a seated figure with a jackal's head as classifier.

sentences.l: (?) · you · know · the-name · of · door · this · so-as-to · tell · ꜥšꜣ(?) · to-me
sentences.i: Do you know the name of this door, to tell it to me?
sentences.n: iw·k rḫ·tw 'you know': iw with ·k, and the stative of rḫ with the 2nd singular ending ·tw (t, w). The ir in front (reed, stroke, mouth) is taken as bringing in the question, as Budge takes it; it could also be 'if'. sbꜣ 'door' is the gateway sign alone. Budge reads it sebeχ, as if sbḫt 'portal'; but pn 'this' (stool p, water n) is masculine and agrees with sbꜣ 'door'. r ḏd 'so as to say' is r + infinitive. The lizard with plural strokes (ꜥšꜣ 'many') makes no clear sense here; Budge leaves it untranslated. Knowing names is the theme of all that follows: the dead may pass a door only if he can name it.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · scribe · Ani · true-of-voice · in · peace · true-of-voice
sentences.i: Words spoken by the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice in peace, true of voice:
sentences.n: The same formula as at the start, here not in red; ḥtp is spelled in full this time, the offering table with t and p.

sentences.l: (…) this · Kher-sek-Shu · the-name · of · door · this
sentences.i: (…) this. 'Kher-sek-Shu' is the name of this door.
sentences.n: Here Budge goes back from Plate 30 to Plate 29, and line 19 opens with pn 'this' standing alone: nothing before it on the papyrus, as printed, gives it a noun, and it may be the end of a phrase the scribe left out. The answer is a sentence of two nouns side by side, 'A (is) the name of B'. ḫr-sk-šw joins two of Budge's groups as one name: placenta ḫ, mouth r, bolt s, the sk sign with k, and the low sign printed U15 for the forearm with stick; then šw, Shu (the feather šw, w, and a god who on the papyrus wears a feather — the type gives a plain seated god, an approximation). sk means 'wipe away, destroy', ḫr 'fall' or 'under'; the name's sense is not clear.

sentences.l: said · by · the-majesty · of · Anubis
sentences.i: Words spoken by the Majesty of Anubis:
sentences.n: ḏd in is in red again. The stroke printed above the n belongs to ḥm 'majesty' (written with it on line 17); it is kept where the print sets it and read as part of ḥm. Budge's transliteration has 'an' without its accent here, perhaps a broken letter.

sentences.l: (?) · you · know · the-name · of · leaf(?) · upper · leaf(?) · lower
sentences.i: Do you know the name of the upper leaf and of the lower leaf (of the door)?
sentences.n: The question of line 17 again. stm (Budge: setem) is a small two-leaved sprig, m, and a curved arrow-tipped stroke taken as a wood classifier; the word is not otherwise known, and from the context it names a part of the door — its upper and lower leaf or panel — but neither its reading nor its meaning is secure. ḥry 'upper' (the face ḥr, r, y and the sky as classifier) is Budge's restoration of damage. ẖry 'lower' is the butcher's block ẖr with r, y and the papyrus roll. The numeral of line 22 stands inside the first stm in Budge's print.

sentences.l: lord · of-Maat · who-is-upon · top · feet · his-two · (is) · the-name · of · leaf · upper
sentences.i: 'Lord of Maat, who is upon his two feet' is the name of the upper leaf;
sentences.n: Ani answers without a ḏd in. nb mꜣꜥt 'Lord of Maat' (basket nb; plinth mꜣꜥ, t, papyrus roll and plural strokes). ḥry tp, 'who is upon', is the nisba ḥry with tp 'head, top' (the head and stroke); rd·fy is the two legs with ·f and the dual y, 'his two feet'. in (reed, water) before rn is unexpected: it may be the particle in that marks the predicate ('it is …'), or a slip; it is rendered 'is'. stmt has a t this time.

morph.gloss: (particle) it is — here apparently marking the predicate (?)

sentences.l: lord · of-strength · marshaller · of-the-herds
sentences.i: 'Lord of strength, who marshals the herds' (is the name of the lower one).
sentences.n: The papyrus does not repeat 'is the name of the lower leaf': it is understood, and Budge supplies it in brackets. pḥty 'strength' is the hind-quarters pḥ, t, y and two lion's foreparts; ṯsw (the knotted cloth ṯs, s, w, and the low sign printed U15 for the forearm with stick) is from ṯs 'tie, raise up, marshal', 'one who marshals'. mnmnt 'cattle, herds' is the gaming-board mn with n, written twice, t, a bull and plural strokes. The numeral of line 25 stands inside mnmnt in Budge's print.

sentences.l: pass · yourself · you · know · Osiris · scribe · accounting · of-the-god's-offerings · of · gods · all · of-Thebes · Ani · true-of-voice · possessor · of-honour
sentences.i: Pass, then, for you know (it), Osiris, accounting scribe of the god's offerings of all the gods of Thebes, Ani, true of voice, possessor of honour.
sentences.n: Anubis lets him through. sš (bolt s, pool š, crossed sticks, walking legs) is taken as the imperative 'pass, go through'; the verb is not certain. ir·k is the preposition r with ·k, written with a reed before it, used after an imperative for emphasis ('pass, you!'). twk 'you' (t, w, k) is a later form of the independent pronoun, the subject of the stative rḫ·tw 'you know'. wsir again puts the eye first. sš ḥsb 'accounting scribe': ḥsb 'reckon' is a single round sign (coded Aa2 from the print) with the papyrus roll. ḥtp-nṯr 'the god's offerings' joins two of Budge's groups as one word: the offering table ḥtp with t and p, and the god's flag with the seated god. nṯrw nbw 'all the gods' (nb with plural strokes is 'every, all'); wꜣst 'Thebes' is the wꜣs-sceptre with t and the town sign. nb imꜣḫ 'possessor of honour': imꜣḫ (the backbone sign with its stroke) is the honoured state of the blessed dead. Here Budge's text of Ani stops and he prints an Appendix from another papyrus (Naville's), which is not on Ani's papyrus.

morph.gloss: (after an imperative) yourself, then — r with a suffix, written ir
